title: Static Twin Screw Wooden Hand Clamp
description: One newly authored complete static wooden handscrew clamp in a fixed laid-down open pose. Two full elongated timber jaws each have two actual through pockets with complete captured square-to-round bushings. Two parallel steel spindles have separate opposite-side timber grips and continuous fixed visual helical ridges; an empty front gripping bay extends beyond the front spindle. This whole double-spindle wood-jaw apparatus has no long steel guide bar, sliding F-jaw or table-edge C mount, and does not reuse or recolour the old F clamp or bench vise. Twelve separately editable closed meshes, three opaque solid PBR materials, metres, native Z-up and full horizontal bounds-centred ground origin. One prop, zero scenes. Fixed visual only: no stock, bench interface, working threads, jaw adjustment, clamping force, machining, fit standard, durability, load or safety claim. Bushes and shaft ridges intentionally fixed, not a real bearing/thread tolerance proof.
